newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya students clash with police outside Nairobi.
newsitem.headline: Kenya students clash with police outside Nairobi.

text.p: About 100 university students clashed with riot police at a campus just outside Kenya's capital on Friday, the second consecutive day of student unrest, witnesses said.
President Daniel arap Moi meanwhile warned against what he called "a new culture of violence" in Kenya's politics, saying it threatened the very fabric that held the country together.

Witnesses said up to 70 riot police, firing rubber bullets and teargas, skirmished with stone-throwing students at the Lower Kabete campus of Nairobi University but clashes were smaller than on Thursday.
One student was slightly wounded by a rubber bullet at Kabete.
About a dozen policemen were hurt on Thursday and cars were stoned as Nairobi University students battled riot police on the main highway through the city centre for several hours.
The students were protesting against a proposed government bill calling for the expulsion of those who fail to pay fees.
"There is no justice in what the government is doing. Education will be only for the rich," a student leader who declined to be named said at Kabate on Friday.

Moi, in power since 1978, is widely expected to win presidential and parliamentary elections this year, pitting the ruling Kenya African National Union against opposition parties divided along ethnic and personal lines.

Speaking on Friday at a fund-raising event in western Kenya, Moi warned that non-governmental organisations (NGOs) "meddling" in Kenya's political affairs risked being deregistered, which would mean they could no longer operate.
He singled out the National Council of NGOs as involving itself in politics and added that it was bent on fomenting trouble in the country and was also subverting law and order.

Opposition groups and other bodies, including the National Council of NGOs, demanding constitutional reforms before the poll have called nationwide rallies for Monday. No date has yet been set for the general elections.
